historical_flood_events.cause: Nag River overflow; inadequate stormwater system; encroachment on Nag River; Eichhornia (water hyacinth) blockage at Ambazari Lake outfalls
historical_flood_events.relief_announced: ₹10,000 per affected family; ₹5,00,000 for affected business owners

historical_flood_events.note: Historic design-storm event, used as the storm rainfall basis in the VNIT susceptibility study
Heavy rains, waterlogging, disrupted traffic across Nagpur/Vidarbha

historical_flood_events.impact: Submerged underpasses, school children rescued by excavators, vehicles stuck under railway underpasses, airport connectivity cut off, roads submerged for hours
historical_flood_events.cause_per_press: Blocked drains, encroachment on natural water channels, incomplete civic works; poorly planned cement-concrete road projects built without stormwater drainage; raised road levels above adjoining properties; nullahs narrowed/encroached
historical_flood_events.accountability_angle: RTI filed by activist Abhay Kolarkar (published ~2 weeks before this data pull) got NMC to confirm crores were spent desilting the Nag, Pili, and Pohra rivers ahead of the 2026 monsoon, with ~₹4.95 crore budgeted for 2026-27 drain-cleaning specifically — yet the city flooded catastrophically days/weeks later. Press (The Hitavada, 30 Jul 2026) is explicitly asking whether pre-monsoon desilting was actually completed and who should be held accountable. This is the strongest real-world justification for CivicProof: it shows the exact 'spending happened but nobody can verify the work' gap the hash-anchoring layer is designed to close.

post_2023_flood_government_response.sanctioned_for: nullah desilting, road repairs, 5 new pumping stations

wards_38_prabhags: NOTE: These are NMC's official 38 prabhag boundary descriptions (landmark-based, not lat/lng polygons). Useful for (a) labeling citizen reports by ward name, (b) manually geocoding key landmarks in QGIS to approximate ward polygons if time allows, (c) matching your synthetic drain network to real named areas. Full boundary text for all 38 wards was extracted from Nagpur Today's published list. Key ward area names by number: 1=Panjara Colony/Shuddhodhan Nagar, 4=Bharat Nagar, 7=Bezonbagh, 9=Chhaoni, 13=Ambazari Tank area, 14=Ramnagar/Civil Lines, 15=Dhantoli, 17=Ajni, 18=Sakkardara, 21=Shanti Nagar, 23=Bhandewadi, 24=Chikhli, 25=Wathoda/Sakkardara Lake, 27=Seminary Hills/Sadar, 29=Vayusena Nagar, 31=Dharampeth/Ambazari Lake, 32=VNIT Campus/Hingna Road, 35=Manewada/Hudkeshwar, 36=Airport/Sonegaon, 38=Butibori boundary/MIHAN

vnit_frequency_ratio_model._note: Full parameter tables from Gaurkhede & Adane (2023). FR = Frequency Ratio; higher = stronger correlation with historical flooding. Use these directly as weights in your risk_score formula (Section H of your master plan).
